verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; no STOP (no confirmed UB left unrepaired, no ABI regression, no hidden obligation and no remaining unsafe-safe-Rust API); four # Safety-contract repairs and one allocator-seam coordinate repair
scope: Per-file contract audit of the OCSP CERTID builder/comparators, OCSP text printers, OCSP responder builders, the five OCSP extension tables and callbacks, the seven param_build_set two-way writers, OSSL_PARAM_dup/merge/free (including the secure-block terminator), OSSL_PARAM_allocate_from_text/print_to_bio, and PEM_ASN1_read_bio. evp/method_store.rs was deferred as the method-store registry boundary; pem/pem_oth.rs was substituted from the head of the stable queue. OCSP and PEM payloads are public data; params temporaries may carry key material and are classified SECRET_DATA where applicable. No constant-time claim is made for any file from source inspection.

files_not_run.reason: Method-store registry and OSSL_METHOD_CONSTRUCT_METHOD dispatch boundary (store locking, construct/reserve/unreserve callbacks, method cache). Deferred for a dedicated boundary audit; it remains in REMAINING-AUDIT.txt at the head of the queue.

defects.class: unsafe # Safety contract permits a NULL the body dereferences
defects.description: OCSP_cert_to_id said subject and issuer may each be NULL, but issuer is read for its subject name and public-key bit string; OCSP_cert_id_new said issuerName/issuerKey may be NULL, but X509_NAME_digest requires a live name and the EVP_Digest arm reads (*issuerKey).data unconditionally.
defects.fix: Contracts now require a live issuer carrying a public-key bit string and live (non-NULL) issuerName/issuerKey. serialNumber, subject and dgst retain their NULL-allowed forms, which the bodies handle. No code or ABI change.
defects.witness: Source comparison with crypto/ocsp/ocsp_lib.c:22-90; focused ocsp:: 1 passed and the full library suite pass.

defects.class: unsafe # Safety contract understates the readable extent of a _PTR entry
defects.description: ossl_param_dup's contract required each data field to be readable for its data_size, but OSSL_PARAM_OCTET_PTR/OSSL_PARAM_UTF8_PTR entries read one full *const c_void from data, and data_size describes the pointed-to string rather than the pointer storage.
defects.fix: The contract now requires the _PTR arm's data to be aligned and readable for one pointer, and keeps data_size readability for every non-_PTR entry. No code change.
defects.witness: Source comparison with crypto/params_dup.c:96-126; focused params:: 53 passed and the full library suite pass.

defects.class: unsafe # Safety contract permits a NULL the body dereferences
defects.description: has_hex_prefix documented s as NULL-or-NUL-terminated but dereferenced s immediately; a caller following the contract could pass NULL and cause UB.
defects.fix: Contract now requires non-NULL and NUL-terminated. No code change.
defects.witness: Source comparison with HAS_PREFIX in crypto/params_from_text.c:35; focused params:: 53 passed.

defects.class: unsafe # Safety contract omits a readable-extent precondition
defects.description: OSSL_PARAM_allocate_from_text documented value as NUL-terminated, but the non-hex OSSL_PARAM_OCTET_STRING arm copies value_n bytes, which need not include a terminator.
defects.fix: Contract now states value must be NUL-terminated for the string forms and readable for value_n bytes for the octet-string form. No code change.
defects.witness: Source comparison with crypto/params_from_text.c:307-334; focused params:: 53 passed.

defects.description: Both modules passed the bare translation-unit path and line 0 to CRYPTO_zalloc/CRYPTO_secure_zalloc/CRYPTO_free/CRYPTO_secure_clear_free. The authority's plain .c units carry the ../../src/openssl-3.6.4/ __FILE__ prefix, and each allocation/release has its own line; the file and line are forwarded to a caller-installed CRYPTO_set_mem_functions hook.
defects.fix: FILE now uses the admitted build's prefixed spelling; dup uses alloc :46, failed-duplicate free :133, merge alloc :191, secure free :240, array free :241; from_text uses alloc :325 and failure free :332. OwnedParamBlock stores its release line and OwnedBuf::new_zeroed_released separates from_text's alloc/release coordinates. No size, layout, export or signature changed.
defects.witness: Source comparison with crypto/params_dup.c:46,133,191,240,241 and crypto/params_from_text.c:325,332; compiled and focused tests pass. No allocator-coordinate differential harness exists for these units (NOT_RUN).

allocator_coordinate_changes: src/params/dup.rs: FILE c"crypto/params_dup.c" -> c"../../src/openssl-3.6.4/crypto/params_dup.c"; LINE 0 -> 46 (buf alloc), 133 (failed duplicate free), 191 (merge alloc), 240 (secure free), 241 (array free)
contracts_reused: OB-1 OwnedBuf: validated single release, including new_zeroed_released's explicit allocation/release coordinate pair
OB-4 secure-block terminator: OSSL_PARAM_ALLOCATED_END == 127 carries the secure block and its size, and OSSL_PARAM_free releases it with CRYPTO_secure_clear_free before the public array
C ABI caller contracts: NULL-or-live optional pointers, caller-sized buffers and caller-terminated key arrays
BIGNUM ownership: BN_asc2bn/BN_hex2bn produce a live BIGNUM that the caller releases with BN_free on every arm
ASN.1 item ownership: OCSP_*_new / OCSP_*_free and ASN1_item_* produce or consume whole values
CRYPTO_* allocator seam at the authority's exact size/file/line, now including the prefixed plain-.c __FILE__ spelling
residuals: src/evp/method_store.rs remains the deferred method-store registry boundary.

OSSL_PARAM_allocate_from_text's failure path plainly frees a buffer that OPENSSL_hexstr2buf_ex may have partially filled with parameter text; the authority does the same. A cleansing release would be a deliberate improvement and is a hardening candidate.

from_text's q.data_size * 8 range test can overflow on a hostile descriptor: a debug build panics (caught by guard_ffi), the release build wraps as the authority does. Hardening candidate, not a reachable memory-safety defect.
OSSL_PARAM_print_to_bio does not free the BIGNUM that OSSL_PARAM_get_BN allocates for a wide integer, matching the authority's own leak; recorded rather than silently changed.

The OCSP printers and builders retain the authority's unconditional dereference of mandatory decoded members (certStatus, thisUpdate, requestList entries), which a successful ASN.1 decode establishes.
No constant-time claim is made for the OCSP or PEM units from source inspection.
